Chapter 208: How Much is ByteDance Worth Now? (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Leader mjiangsuga)

"Hey, ancient costumes aren't worn with black silk stockings."

"You didn't change into a dudou either."

"I'm starting to think you're a bit of a pervert!"

"It's called adding a little spice."

"Turn around. I'll call you when I'm ready."

"I'll help you put it on."

"No, I'll do it myself."

In the hotel room, Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue were exchanging tips on Hanfu styling.

Bian Guanyue was always bashful at first, but would get wild halfway through, even proactively trying all sorts of new things.

Chen Guiliang obediently turned his back, listening to the rustling sounds behind him.

After two or three minutes, Bian Guanyue finally said, "I'm ready."

Chen Guiliang turned his head and his eyes immediately lit up.

She was just too good at this!

Not only did she lift the lower garment to faintly reveal the black silk stockings, but her upper body was also intentionally disheveled, giving her a pitiable look with her cloud-like hair in disarray.

Especially with the gaze she'd practiced since elementary school for Chinese opera, a single glance from under lowered brows was enough to steal one's soul.

Chen Guiliang sidled up to her with a grin.

Bian Guanyue pushed him away. "General, you must not."

Still playing roles?

So Chen Guiliang played along with her. "And why must I not?"

Bian Guanyue said, "This humble servant already belongs to Grand Preceptor Dong. A wise minister does not serve two masters, how can one woman marry two husbands?"

So they were playing Lü Bu and Diaochan.

Chen Guiliang went to embrace her. "Dong Zhuo is a treacherous villain! No need to observe proprieties for him. Besides, your father promised you to me, Lü Fengxian, first!"

"The General and the Grand Chancellor are father and son," Bian Guanyue took half a step back, intentionally pulling at her sleeve to half-reveal a fragrant shoulder. "I have already married the father, I cannot then marry the son."

Chen Guiliang forced himself on her like an overlord. "I, Lü Bu, have roamed the world. When have I ever cared for what others think, or for matters of propriety? Today, I will take back what is mine!"

Bian Guanyue let herself be pushed down, feigning resistance. "Don't let the Grand Chancellor find out," she said in a fluster.

"I'm not afraid even if he does."

"The Grand Chancellor is here."

"Let him listen from outside."

It was a great battle, thoroughly satisfying.

Bian Guanyue struggled the entire time, growing more excited the more she struggled, constantly crying out for the Grand Chancellor to save her.

After the battle, they took a shower and came back to cuddle and chat.

Bian Guanyue said, "That Chinese style of yours, I could force myself to write something like it, but it always feels very awkward. This month, I downloaded a lot of songs to listen to, and I think I've found a direction."

"What direction?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue said, "Lo Ta-yu's 'Homesick Four Rhymes.' I never thought it was that amazing before. Listening to it this time felt completely different, especially the intro and the interlude, which perfectly blend traditional Chinese music with modern music. Some parts don't follow the meter of Western music theory, but you can't even tell unless you listen closely."

"So you had an epiphany?" Chen Guiliang didn't understand what she was talking about.

Bian Guanyue said, "It was as if a great door had been opened. But the more I peek inside, the more I realize my own ignorance. Whether it's traditional music or Western music, my foundations are too weak. This winter break, I want to go back to Rongcheng to visit folk opera artists and learn a few things from them."

Chen Guiliang encouraged her, "That's a good thing. You'll become a great musician in the future."

Bian Guanyue smiled. "I'm no genius. Next summer break, I'll go to Jiangnan to learn some Kunqu opera. Sichuan opera also has Kunqiang melodies, and I want to know how they differ from Kunqu. For future vacations, I'll go learn Huangmei opera, Pingtan, Cantonese opera... I don't need to learn them in-depth, just get a general understanding. After that, I'll go study Western music theory."

Chen Guiliang was surprised. "You've found your calling?"

"I'm not sure if it's a calling, the thought just suddenly came to me," Bian Guanyue said. "The composition and arrangement of 'Homesick Four Rhymes' felt like a sword manual from an unparalleled master. I know it's incredible, and I can understand parts of it, but to fully grasp it, I need to improve myself."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Maybe Lo Ta-yu just had a moment of inspiration. He was only in his early twenties when he wrote that song."

"Perhaps," Bian Guanyue said. "After I graduate from my undergraduate studies, I want to apply for a master's degree in music or opera theory. Since you've helped me invest in a game company, I won't be short on money. It's the perfect opportunity to do those non-profitable jobs, collecting and researching all sorts of folk tunes. And those folk songs, so many Sichuan folk songs can't be heard anymore."

The more Bian Guanyue spoke, the more excited she became. "Once I've collected a decent amount of Sichuan folk songs, I'll go to Yunnan and Guizhou, then to Jing-Hu. After I'm done visiting the south, I'll head north and continue. It will definitely be very interesting!"

Chen Guiliang said, "I actually know how to sing a folk song from Caiyun Province."

"Really?" Bian Guanyue was quite surprised.

"I'll sing it for you."

Chen Guiliang suppressed a laugh and began to sing, "Old driver, give me a ride, I need to go to Kuncheng..."

Before he could finish the classic folk song, Bian Guanyue was laughing so hard she was punching him. "That's a dirty song!"

"This is popular art, it's very popular in Caiyun Province," Chen Guiliang said.

"You think I'd believe you?"

"The truth speaks for itself. You'll find out when you go there to collect folk songs in the future."

"Pfft, you're full of lies."

Bian Guanyue really did go back to Rongcheng. She wanted to use her winter break to visit folk opera artists.

ByteDance and Game Science soon held their annual parties, which were also an opportunity to hand out bonuses.

At this time in China, foreign companies from Europe and America generally gave regular employees a "year-end double salary plus a one to three-month bonus." In other words, they would receive two to four extra months of salary at the end of the year.

Top-tier private enterprises didn't have a double salary system, instead giving performance-based bonuses equivalent to one to six months of salary.

Monopolistic state-owned enterprises gave an extra three to six months' salary.

Ordinary state-owned enterprises gave an extra one to three months' salary.

Japanese, Korean, and Taiwanese companies were very stingy, no better than ordinary state-owned enterprises.

Although Chen Guiliang's company wasn't large, it gave out year-end bonuses on par with the top domestic private enterprises. And even though ByteDance was tight on funds, it gave out generous year-end bonuses as well.

The annual party also had a legitimate raffle, the kind where no one was allowed to cheat!

The raffle box had to be transparent.

The junior employees would draw first, and any employee could stir the box, making it difficult for the company's senior management to cheat even if they wanted to.

At ByteDance.

Hou Qiao, an advertising salesperson who had been with the company for just over four months, hadn't really paid much mind to the raffle. She had never won any big prize in her life. She casually picked a slip and returned to her seat.

"Sigh, I knew it. It's got to be the guaranteed consolation prize," lamented Jiang Jiajie to her left.

Yuan Hao, on her right, said, "I did a tiny bit better than you, a fifth prize."

"Hou Qiao, what about you?" Jiang Jiajie asked.

Hou Qiao replied as she unfolded the slip, "I guess it's about the same... Uh..."

"What's wrong?"

Jiang Jiajie and Yuan Hao both leaned over to look.

"AH!!!!!!"

Hou Qiao let out a sharp, ear-piercing scream, jumping up and down and cheering, "Grand prize! Grand prize! I won the grand prize!"

The grand prize was the right to use a Chery QQ.

It was the "right to use" because the state had enacted a law prohibiting raffles from giving away large items like cars.

"CEO Chen, CEO Chen!"

Hou Qiao ran over, waving the grand prize slip. "I won the grand prize!"

As she passed, her colleagues cast envious gazes her way.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Congratulations, congratulations. You're the company's lucky star. You'll definitely bring everyone good luck next year."

Hou Qiao said gleefully, "I can't drive, and I rent a place nearby. This car is useless to me. Can I exchange it for cash?"

"You can," Chen Guiliang nodded and said.

He hadn't bought the car yet anyway, and a junker like that only cost a few tens of thousands of yuan.

"First prize! I won a first prize!"

Ding Qiang, one of the first programmers to join the company, was so excited he jumped on the spot. "Haha, I can get a new computer."

The first prize winner could choose their prize, and one of the options was a high-spec computer.

Excited shouts kept erupting.

There was only one grand prize, but there were three first prizes, five second prizes...

With just over a hundred people in the whole company, the probability of winning was quite high.

Chen Guiliang said with a smile, "Colleagues who won the big prizes, please come up on stage and share your thoughts. The grand prize winner first."

Hou Qiao was in a state of excitement. She said emotionally, "I graduated from a vocational school and came from the countryside. It's hard to make it in Beijing... I drifted between a few companies for several years, never getting anywhere. If things had continued like that, I was planning to go back to my hometown, get married, and have kids. At my previous company, my supervisor was especially mean to me..."

As Hou Qiao spoke of her grievances, her voice started to break, and she wiped away tears. "It was only when I came to ByteDance that I found a sense of belonging! All my colleagues here are so nice. I've only been working here for four months, and I thought I wouldn't get a year-end bonus, but the company still gave me a one-month bonus..."

"My previous companies also had raffles, but the big prizes always went to the managers or someone with connections... I never thought I could win the grand prize..."

She wiped her tears again and bowed to the audience. "Thank you, CEO Chen. Thank you to all the leaders and colleagues... I will definitely work my hardest from now on and help the company bring in more advertising. I won't let down my leaders' guidance or my colleagues' care... Go, Hou Qiao, you can do it!"

Chen Guiliang scratched his forehead.

This employee spoke as if she were on stimulants, making it feel like a pyramid scheme rally.

Next was Ding Qiang, who had been the first to draw a first prize. "I'm not very good with words, but I want to thank everyone in the company. I was the first employee to join ByteDance through recruitment. Over this past year, not only has my salary increased, but more importantly, I've learned new skills and can now handle more difficult work. I work hard every day, and I study every day after work... I will grow with the company, until the day I'm too old to work!"

*Clap clap clap!*

Thunderous applause erupted.

Ding Qiang was very well-liked in the company, partly because he was a veteran employee, and partly because he had an honest and kind personality and was willing to help colleagues.

Of course, there were some who didn't like him, feeling that the guy was too much of a try-hard.

Well, the term "involution" hadn't been invented yet.

After the annual party, Chang Zhongxiang, who was in charge of finance, found Chen Guiliang. "After the Spring Festival, we should start trying to contact venture capitalists. The monthly costs are getting higher and higher, and the company's funds can only last another four or five months."

"Go ahead and contact them. IDG and DJ are probably getting antsy too," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang was very much looking forward to ByteDance's current valuation.

He even anticipated it would be over 100 million US dollars!

(End of this chapter)
